Subject: Re: DPA redlines — proposed carve‑out language

Team — draft language below that attempts to bridge both sides. Highlights: (1) flat prohibition on using Customer Content to train or fine‑tune models or derive model weights; (2) explicit carve‑out for aggregated, non‑identifiable telemetry used solely for service reliability/metrics; (3) audit right language for enforcement.

Proposed clause (to insert into Section 4):

"Training and Model Improvement. Provider shall not use Customer Content to train, fine‑tune, or otherwise improve the parameters, weights, or underlying representations of any generative or foundation models where such resulting model artifacts could be attributed to or reproduce Customer Content. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may collect and use aggregated, de‑identified telemetry and usage metrics (e.g., latency, error rates, token counts, feature usage) for purposes of monitoring, debugging, capacity planning, and improving the operational quality of the Service, provided that such telemetry cannot be used to reconstruct Customer Content or individual user data."

I also recommend adding: "Provider will maintain technical and organizational measures to prevent retention of Customer Content for the purposes of long‑term model training absent Customer's prior written consent."

If that looks acceptable, Nikhil/Karthik can propose it back to Acme. I think it should satisfy legal while preserving necessary operational telemetry.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
